Finally, I'm computing the global minimum failed row (or n if no failure) across ranks via MPI_Allreduce with MPI_MIN, since each rank processes rows in order and can only record one failure.\n\nNow I'm writing a validation function that reconstructs L*L^T per owned row and compares against the original matrix, tracking max absolute and relative error...\n\nStill writing validation logic...\n\nNow I'm starting on the main function, initializing MPI and getting rank and size.\n\nI'm working through the argument parsing logic, handling unknown flags and the help option, setting up a status code that determines whether to continue running or exit early with a finalize call.\n\nNow I'm sketching the matrix allocation on each rank and thinking through how to distribute row ownership across ranks for an n×n matrix, computing how many rows each rank owns.\n\nI'm adding logic to copy each process's originally owned rows into a backup buffer when validation is enabled, then timing the distributed Cholesky computation with a barrier before it starts and recording duration after the result reduces across ranks.\n\nIf the failed row index is less than n, I print the positive-definiteness error and failure message matching the original ordering, and set the exit code to 1. Otherwise I print timing and gigaflops stats on the root process, optionally print the result matrix, and if validation is requested, run validateCholesky and print PASSED/FAILED while setting the exit code accordingly.\n\nI'm also handling edge cases like n=0 producing NaN gflops (matching the original), finalizing MPI before returning, and casting carefully between size_t and int for ownership and broadcast calls to avoid sign-comparison warnings.\n\nOne thing I need to think through: with nonblocking broadcasts under Open MPI's default libnbc implementation, progress only happens when a process makes MPI calls—so the root's pending sends won't actually advance until it hits another MPI call itself.\n\nThis creates a real pipeline issue: intermediate nodes in the broadcast tree only forward data when they progress, meaning if a rank is busy computing its own row with no MPI calls in between, its forwarding to children stalls entirely during that computation window.\n\nA mitigation would be inserting lightweight progress calls, like a cheap MPI_Iprobe, periodically during the column loop to nudge the MPI engine without significant overhead relative to the dot product work, keeping the broadcast tree flowing even while compute is happening.\n\nSince I can't test on a real cluster, I'll just try this on my 256-core box with mpirun at -np 4 and 8. Maybe it's simpler to sidestep the libnbc tree-forwarding issue entirely by having each owner send its row directly to every other rank with point-to-point calls instead.\n\nI keep running into the same progress-engine issue with rendezvous sends needing sender-side progress, even with direct point-to-point messaging, so for small process counts that's still fine. I'll stick with Ibcast but add periodic progress nudges via Iprobe every 32 columns in the loop—it's a bit of a hack, but I'll measure performance first and only add it if needed.\n\nI'm updating the CMake file to find MPI, link the MPI C++ library plus math, and keep the project using both C and C++ languages since FindMPI works fine either way. Now writing the file.\n\n","time":{"start":1793067769487,"end":1793067798765},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I'll keep the per-element arithmetic order identical, so the parallel version should produce bit-identical output to this reference.\n\nMy plan:\n- **Distribution:** row-cyclic. Row `i` is owned by rank `i % P`. Each rank keeps a full copy of L.\n- **Pipelining:** each finished row is broadcast with `MPI_Ibcast`. A rank waits on row `j` only when it first needs it, so rows overlap in a wavefront.\n- **Generation and validation:** every rank regenerates B from the same seed (cheap, O(n²)), computes only its own rows of B·Bᵀ, and validates its own rows of L·Lᵀ, with max-reductions.\n\nNow I'll write the new source.","time":{"start":1793067798769,"end":1793067798786}}}
{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793067811574,"sessionID":"ses_e84d7bc1dffe0bHvjijw1lMpOl","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_0197QaTH7z6Ynedzz4RaTVsL","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r4/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Distributed-memory Cholesky decomposition (MPI).\n//\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular.\n// The matrix is stored in row-major order.\n//\n// Parallelization:\n//  - Rows are distributed cyclically: row i is owned by rank (i % size).\n//  - Every rank keeps a full copy of the matrix buffer, so the final factor L is\n//    available everywhere (needed for output and validation).\n//  - Row i is final once its owner has computed it. The owner then broadcasts the\n//    lower part (i+1 entries) with MPI_Ibcast. Other ranks wait for a row only when\n//    they first need it, so rows are factored in a pipelined wavefront.\n//  - Each element is computed with exactly the same sequence of floating-point\n//    operations as the sequential algorithm, so results are bit-identical for any\n//    number of ranks.\n\nnamespace {\n\ninline int ownerOf(const size_t row, const int size) {\n    return static_cast<int>(row % static_cast<size_t>(size));\n}\n\n// Number of rows owned by `rank` in an n-row matrix.\ninline size_t numOwnedRows(const size_t n, const int rank, const int size) {\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    if (r >= n) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n    return (n - r - 1) / static_cast<size_t>(size) + 1;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix. Every rank regenerates the same\n// random matrix B (seed 42) and computes only the rows it owns.\n// If fullRows is false, only the lower triangle (j <= i) of owned rows is filled,\n// which is all the factorization reads.\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n, const int rank, const int size,\n                                    const bool fullRows) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute owned rows of A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(rank); i < n; i += static_cast<size_t>(size)) {\n        const size_t jEnd = fullRows ? n : i + 1;\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < jEnd; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(rank); i < n; i += static_cast<size_t>(size)) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\n// Collective. Factorizes A in place (row-major, lower triangular result, upper part zeroed).\n// Every rank must hold the full buffer A on entry (owned rows filled, others unused).\n// Returns the smallest row index whose pivot was not positive, or n on success.\nsize_t choleskyDistributed(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n, const int rank, const int size) {\n    std::vector<MPI_Request> reqs(n, MPI_REQUEST_NULL);\n    std::vector<char> ready(n, 0);  // row is available locally (owned or already received)\n    size_t failedRow = n;\n    bool failed = false;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        const int owner = ownerOf(i, size);\n\n        if (owner == rank) {\n            ready[i] = 1;\n            if (!failed) {\n                double* Ai = &A[i * n];\n                for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n                    if (j < i && !ready[j]) {\n                        // Row j is needed for this column: wait for its broadcast.\n                        MPI_Wait(&reqs[j], MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);\n                        ready[j] = 1;\n                    }\n\n                    const double* Aj = &A[j * n];\n                    double sum = 0.0;\n\n                    if (i == j) {\n                        // Diagonal element\n                        for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                            sum += Ai[k] * Ai[k];\n                        }\n                        const double val = Ai[j] - sum;\n                        if (val <= 0.0) {\n                            // Matrix is not positive definite\n                            failedRow = i;\n                            failed = true;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                        Ai[j] = sqrt(val);\n                    } else {\n                        // Off-diagonal element\n                        for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                            sum += Ai[k] * Aj[k];\n                        }\n                        Ai[j] = (Ai[j] - sum) / Aj[j];\n                    }\n                }\n\n                // Zero out upper triangular part\n                for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n                    Ai[j] = 0.0;\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Publish the finished row (lower part, i+1 entries) to all ranks.\n            MPI_Ibcast(&A[i * n], static_cast<int>(i + 1), MPI_DOUBLE, owner, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &reqs[i]);\n        } else {\n            // Post the receive for a row owned by another rank. The data is\n            // written directly into this rank's copy of the matrix.\n            MPI_Ibcast(&A[i * n], static_cast<int>(i + 1), MPI_DOUBLE, owner, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &reqs[i]);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // All broadcasts must complete before the factor is used or the buffers are released.\n    MPI_Waitall(static_cast<int>(n), reqs.data(), MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE);\n\n    // Upper part of rows received from other ranks was never written and stays zero.\n\n    // Agree on the first failing row (identical on all ranks).\n    long long localFail = failed ? static_cast<long long>(failedRow) : static_cast<long long>(n);\n    long long globalFail = localFail;\n    MPI_Allreduce(&localFail, &globalFail, 1, MPI_LONG_LONG, MPI_MIN, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    return static_cast<size_t>(globalFail);\n}\n\n// Collective. Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with the original matrix.\n// A_origOwned holds the original rows owned by this rank (in increasing row order).\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_origOwned, const size_t n,\n                      const int rank, const int size) {\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    // Each rank checks its own rows of L * L^T\n    size_t local = 0;\n    for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(rank); i < n; i += static_cast<size_t>(size), ++local) {\n        const double* Li = &L[i * n];\n        const double* Aorig = &A_origOwned[local * n];\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            const double* Lj = &L[j * n];\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += Li[k] * Lj[k];\n            }\n\n            const double error = fabs(sum - Aorig[j]);\n            maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n            const double rel = error / (fabs(Aorig[j]) + 1e-10);\n            relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n        }\n    }\n\n    double errs[2] = {maxError, relError};\n    MPI_Allreduce(MPI_IN_PLACE, errs, 2, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    maxError = errs[0];\n    relError = errs[1];\n\n    int rank0 = 0;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank0);\n    if (rank0 == 0) {\n        printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n        printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    }\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        if (rank0 == 0) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        }\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    int status = -1;  // -1: continue running; otherwise exit with this code\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) {\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            status = 0;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            status = 1;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (status >= 0) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return status;\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Allocate matrix (full copy on every rank)\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_origOwned;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix (owned rows only)\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    }\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n, rank, size, validate);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        // Save this rank's original rows for validation\n        const size_t numOwned = numOwnedRows(n, rank, size);\n        A_origOwned.resize(numOwned * n);\n        size_t local = 0;\n        for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(rank); i < n; i += static_cast<size_t>(size), ++local) {\n            std::copy_n(&A[i * n], n, &A_origOwned[local * n]);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    }\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    const size_t failedRow = choleskyDistributed(A, n, rank, size);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (failedRow < n) {\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", failedRow);\n            printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        }\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n        double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n        double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n        // Print results for external validation\n        if (printResults) {\n            print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    int exitCode = 0;\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        }\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_origOwned, n, rank, size);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            }\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            }\n            exitCode = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return exitCode;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file {"type":"text","timestamp":1793068522335,"sessionID":"ses_e84d7bc1dffe0bHvjijw1lMpOl","part":{"id":"prt_17b364c67001yZqBLMMrMcDucJ","messageID":"msg_17b36463d001lKLohfxwGTd0FF","sessionID":"ses_e84d7bc1dffe0bHvjijw1lMpOl","type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now always runs under MPI. Only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` changed, and the executable is still `cholesky`.\n\n**Design**\n- **Distribution:** rows are cyclic (row `i` belongs to rank `i % P`). Each rank holds a full copy of L, which the output and validation need.\n- **Pipelining:** each finished row is broadcast with `MPI_Ibcast`. A rank waits for row `j` only when it first needs it, so rows overlap in a wavefront.\n- **Generation and validation:** each rank regenerates B from the same seed, computes only its own rows of B·Bᵀ, and validates its own rows of L·Lᵀ with max-reductions.\n- **Bit-identical results:** each element uses the same operation order as the original, so output matches the sequential reference exactly.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(MPI REQUIRED)` and link `MPI::MPI_CXX`.\n\n**Verification** (Open MPI 4.1.6, GCC 13)\n- Output is identical to the original (sums, hashes, samples, validation) at n=64, 512, and 1000 for 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and 16 ranks.\n- The not-positive-definite path matches the original's message and exit code, tested with a temporarily patched copy outside the workspace.\n- `-h` and unknown-option handling match the original.\n- The build shows no warnings.\n\n**Performance** (wall time of the factorization, original baseline in parentheses)\n\n| n | 1 rank | 4 ranks | 16 ranks | 64 ranks |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 2048 | 2152 ms (2122 ms) | 571 ms | 199 ms | — |\n| 4096 | 18100 ms | 4767 ms | 1324 ms | 691 ms |\n\n- The 16-rank result at n=2048 is about 10.7x the original. Without a periodic progress call the 16-rank time was about 464 ms, so that call was necessary.\n- The n=4096 runs were on a single 256-core node with oversubscription, so they show algorithmic scaling, not real cluster behavior.\n\n**Limitations**\n- Each rank stores the full n×n matrix, so memory per rank does not shrink with P. This limits very large n.\n- Bit-identical results rule out reordering the sums, which blocked or right-looking algorithms would need. That constrains per-core speed, and the speedup comes from the pipeline.\n- The matrix is generated fully on each rank, so generation is cheap but not split across ranks.\n- The progress call (`MPI_Iprobe` every 32 columns) is a tuned constant. It was chosen on this one node and was not swept across other networks or MPI implementations.","time":{"start":1793068518503,"end":1793068522331}}}
